steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Eamon climbed the spiral stairs of Gullpoint Lighthouse just as twilight smudged the horizon. Each night for twenty years, he’d wound the brass mechanism that made the great Fresnel lens revolve, casting a beacon of hope far out at sea. Tonight, though, the wind carried something different—a distant wail, half-washed by crashing waves.

Pausing on the landing, Eamon pressed his hand to the cool stone wall. Far below, a battered fishing boat fought the surf. He flipped open his logbook and jotted a quick note, summoned his oil lamp to burn brighter, then peered through the lookout window. In the dancing glow, he spied a lone figure clinging to a broken mast.

Without hesitation, Eamon descended, grabbed his lantern and life ring, and rushed to the cliff’s edge. “Hold on!” he shouted. The figure’s desperate nod was all the answer he needed. Through swirling spray, he lobbed the ring and hauled the stranger to safety. 

Back in the lantern room, with the storm still raging, Eamon exhaled—and the steady heartbeat of the light above seemed to say that every night, no matter how dark, a single beacon could stave off despair.
